mission.title: Night shift at Tideworks Polytechnic's sealed yard labs
mission.scene: Dry-dock cranes tick past the lab windows while apprentices wait on firmware they cannot send to a cloud chatbot — the yard's IP rules are absolute, and the curriculum is three seasons behind the ships.
mission.briefMd:
## The place

**Tideworks Polytechnic** (fictive port-city college). Yard partners opened a sealed lab corridor: real PLCs, redacted firmware trees, procedure PDFs, safety video. Graduates who can modernize this stack get jobs; toy-kit grads leave town.

IT just racked accelerators after open frontier-scale AI weights became downloadable. Power is on. No learning system exists yet.

## What's strained

- **Skills gap** — manuals lag the ships; no multi-day debug practice on real code under local rules.
- **Outmigration** — serious AI lives on foreign clouds their contracts forbid.
- **Trust** — yard won't leak IP; students won't trust pinout hallucinations.

## A capability that just became more real

Open-weight, near-frontier AI you can host yourself: huge total scale via sparse MoE, ~1M context, vision-in-the-loop, multi-day agentic coding over whole repos. Not a brand ad — the *kind* of advance.

## Your brief

Invent something here that uses that capability. Stakeholder: **Dean Marisol Okonkwo, Applied Engineering**.

## Constraints

Local-only IP. Finite cluster (queue nights). Tests + human gates beat fluent lies. Students own commits. Pilot one track — not the whole port overnight.
